briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 9, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Severe On-the-Ground Impacts and Warnings of Climate Change
sections.content: According to a report released today, global warming has surpassed the 1.5°C threshold, leading to growing global warnings [67]. Domestically, this summer saw 42 heatwaves exceeding 39°C [15], and at Seomang Port in Jindo, a clear phenomenon has been observed where the population of squid, a staple fish, has sharply decreased due to climate change, while yellowtail and tuna populations have seen a reversal [9]. Glacier melt and frequent landslides in the Himalayan region [3, 54], along with severe rainfall in Hawaii and the worsening snow drought in Nevada, clearly demonstrate the gravity of extreme weather events caused by climate change [42, 44]. Furthermore, the occupation of Western Sahara is amplifying climate change risks, and toxic air is being generated by wildfires [63, 66], clearly illustrating that climate change is having widespread and immediate impacts across our lives and ecosystems.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Climate Action and Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Even amidst the climate crisis, positive efforts for climate action and carbon neutrality are continuing both domestically and internationally. Domestically, work has begun on establishing subordinate legislation following the enactment of the Climate Crisis Adaptation Act [20], and cooperation to expand climate action is strengthening, with the Ministry of Climate and the Catholic Archdiocese of Seoul joining hands to respond to the climate crisis [21]. Ansan City successfully hosted the '2026 Ansan Citizens' Environmental Festival' to spread a culture of carbon neutrality [19], and local governments and institutions such as Uljin County and the Cheonan Science and Industry Promotion Agency are practicing carbon neutrality through activities like collecting recyclables and donating clothes [17, 23]. Furthermore, the Korea Energy Agency is actively supporting the overseas expansion of domestic renewable energy companies by participating as the 'Korea Pavilion' in Japan's 'Smart Energy Week 2026' [28, 33], and Vietnam is also accelerating the establishment of an ecosystem to transform into a renewable energy hub [32, 34, 35].

sections.title: 🌍 International Discussions and Challenges for Climate Change Response
sections.content: Responding to climate change is a complex challenge that demands international cooperation and in-depth discussion. The UN is urging joint action to address air pollution and climate change [40], and new global targets such as 'overshoot limitation, peaking, and reduction' are being discussed as key agendas for climate change response [38]. However, legal and economic obstacles to climate change policy implementation persist, as exemplified by the $75 billion climate change superfund bill proposed in New York State being blocked by a federal judge [39]. Furthermore, many people do not clearly recognize the link between climate change and extreme weather events [37], and complex issues in the energy transition process, such as increasing AI power demand and redefining the role of LNG to address renewable energy variability, are also emerging as challenges that need to be resolved [24, 31].

sections.title: 📰 Climate Change and Social Perception & Cultural Responses
sections.content: Climate change is also influencing public perception and cultural responses across society. In the United States, after experiencing a summer of wildfires and record heatwaves, public discussion on climate change is becoming more active [49], but questions are also being raised about the response of leaders. Amidst these changes, individuals and the cultural arts sector are also deepening their awareness of climate change, with people like Linda Brown finding genuine career paths in climate-related fields [52], and bands like Arab Strap addressing climate change in their works [60]. Furthermore, an unusual incident occurred in Colorado where thirsty bears broke into residents' vehicles [47], raising awareness about the unexpected impacts of climate change on wildlife behavior and human society.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the immediate threats of climate change, along with various domestic and international efforts to overcome them, and the complex challenges facing the international community. This is a critical time when continuous attention and action from all of us are urgently needed. This concludes today's climate briefing.
